answer: Sealed second-price bidding stops one operator from flooding the island job board with cheap alias bids. A requester posts a job and each alias submits one sealed price bid in the 48 hour cedar window. The lowest bid wins and is paid the second lowest bid, so ten puppet aliases undercutting gain nothing. The award carries a velvet seal with the alias and funding wallet attached. Two aliases sharing one funding wallet that bid on the same job lose the job and sit out 30 days. A bid below 40 percent of the median bid is flagged and the alias must show past work to bid again.
